facts.text: The Test Square fountain was built in 1732 and carries a carved verse inscription.
The fountain was fed by a cistern that held 1,500 cubic metres of water.
The Test Library was founded in 1740 by the patron whose verse is on the fountain.
The Test Bathhouse took its water from the same cistern from the 18th century onward.
The clock tower's bell was cast in 1803 from the metal of the old fountain's pipes.
The clock tower stands on the site of the patron's first workshop.
The Test Far Gate was rebuilt in 1911.

writer.title: The Patron's Bell

mystery.question: What became of the pipes that fed the old fountain?
mystery.answer: They were melted down and cast into the clock tower's bell in 1803.

writer.briefing: A patron left his mark on these streets, and something of his still rings every hour. Follow what he left behind. Stay on the pavement, daylight only.

places.hint: Look for the big plane tree and the café tables around it.

reveal.text: This fountain was built in 1732, and its carved verse names the man who paid for it.
